resources.string: 1. Open Settings and grant %1$s the overlay permission. This is for displaying an overlay over other apps.
2. Grant %1$s the notification permission (optional). Tapping on the notification will close the overlay and return you to this app.
3. Open Accessibility settings and enable "Middor mirrored input". This is required only when "Enable Touch Controls" is on in Middor settings. Turn touch controls off for a view-only mirror.
4. On the main screen, tap on the "%1$s" button.
5. Ensure that "Single App" is selected, then tap Start. Avoid the "Entire Screen" option, as this will also capture the overlay.
6. Select the application you want to mirror. This will launch the application, create the overlay and post a notification.
7. To exit, tap on the red Close (×) icon in the configured corner of the overlay (top right by default). Alternatively, you can pull down on your status bar and tap the notification.

1. The mirror is fully opaque. Taps, swipes, and multitouch gestures replay at their flipped positions after finger-up, not in real time. Wait for replay before touching again. Enable "Middor mirrored input" in Accessibility settings for touch controls, or turn "Enable Touch Controls" off for a view-only mirror. Touch feedback, tap duration, and the close-button corner are configurable in Settings. Restart the mirror to apply changes.

2. When using the \"Remove System Bars\" setting, the height of the status and navigation bar is recorded before creating the overlay for cropping. If the device orientation changes afterward (e.g. from portrait to landscape), the cropping dimensions will not update.
